items.note: Association named, Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII quoted verbatim, incl. 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern'.

Credited on 'the last clause is the hinge of everything that followed: the station's own figure, with no appeal' plus the story title. Note: the explicit counterfactual ('under payment by weight no one would have lost a dollar') appears only at B3, which cannot travel into A; the causal claim itself is inside A.
Loomis secretary 1901 with the minutes, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager from 1913; 'nephew' and 1911 both rejected.
Station-gain line quoted in full for 1898, annual, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual. Carried to the general account.'
Opened 4 May 1896 on glass borrowed of Larrow Green; 'separator man' and cream to Larrow Green carry the skimming-station substance.
Bench routine: every can weighed, ten-day composite per patron, charge drawn to the mark, hand tester, fat read.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897 (1898 rejected).
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
'nineteen hundredths flat in every month', 'the same in July as in February, which no feed effect does'.

LOST. Section A never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette (none in the county) and so was the one instrument never verified. The nearest statements — 'forty-seven years before anyone had a burette' (D1) and 'the pipette is the standard the plant measures with, and cannot be caught by measuring with itself' (F1) — are outside Section A and cannot travel in.
Keddie b.1861, tester 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
Five columns date/patron/pounds/test/fat, errors struck and initialed, never overwritten.
Summary leaf: 1896 3.80; 1897 part year; 3.61 from 1898 within three hundredths since. Both figures present.
Pipette broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure to 10 July, tests 3.80, back to 3.61, question mark. Nine weeks, not six.
Married Orra Brant, Emmet's sister; Emmet the station's largest patron.
June 1919 circular over Vose's signature; Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement, 'I cannot tell you why the figures are what they are', never took a pound of cream.
Died Feb 1934 'nine years under the imputation'; test book impounded March 1925, Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom wet meadow, six farms (seven rejected), Emmet Brant largest.
Weigh book from 1 Jan 1897, his scale against the station's, 'the two columns agreed for a lifetime'.
1902 complaints present; and the two gaps are kept apart correctly (0.17 vs Larrow Green's 3.78, 0.19 vs the truth of 3.80), at Story 4 and again at E-44.
Grigg's 1908 committee, Jan-Feb-Mar 1908, wet-hay finding reported as the committee's finding and later defeated.

1910 leaf: 200,000 lb on a test of 3.42. Proportionality is enacted inside Section A ('3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60', a 0.18 shortfall, not a flat 0.19) rather than asserted in words; 'the richer herds lost more' and the 4.56/0.24 case sit in F1 outside A. Credited as substance over wording.
To Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958 and returned, Hazel 1962, Rooms 1963.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge, Jerome Cudd. Year does not gate; the 1913 assertion is charged as a corruption deduction instead.
From 1915 four of the six Bottom men hauled over in the summer flush, own station the rest of the year.
REQUIRED (2 of 4) met with room to spare: another county, his own bench, his own glass, and a book never compared with anyone's.
Sixteen seasons 1915-1930 with the season table; 'nineteen hundredths higher on independent glass in another county'.
Same milk off the same wet ground, in the months the hay theory allows no effect; and the cheese-vat argument against watering.
Rosalie Cudd, daughter (niece rejected), took the factory 1941, copied the sixteen seasons off the leaves in 1958; the copies are what reached Ordell County.
Merle Strawn, state inspector, Ordell circuit 1907-1936 (1908 rejected).
Scales and lactometer every visit, never any added water, and told Vose so in 1919.
12 June 1923, ran the pipettes, condemned the whole crate (12 July rejected on the 28 June order).
Credited on the verbatim entry: 'Glass is glass and I did not weigh what it has cost them', with nothing further recorded and the notebook read at the hearing for other lines.
Ordered 28 June, Ammon replied 2 July, new glass in use July 1923, 1924 average 3.80 (3.90 and 3.85 both rejected).

LOST on the strict reading of the bold rule. The crate half is present ('The crate went into the loft over the intake room'), but the item's second bolded element — the notebooks to the state office and, in 1947, to the college library where Ivy found the 1923 volume — is nowhere in the sheet. AMBIGUOUS: the key's own distinctness note describes A6.6's aspect as 'where it went in 1923', under which reading this would score 1. Scored conservatively at 0; a +1 swing if the grader takes the distinctness note as the gate.
January 1925 petition, Emmet Brant's name on it.
Board under Alonzo Frick, three sessions 17 March - 4 May 1925, second and third in the station's weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report read in); 'finds no cause established'.
Four exhibits named, incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook containing the condemnation; 'Nobody laid the second beside the fourth.'
Dismissed 30 April 1925 while the board sat, no cause found; award 4 May 1925, $3,800, without admission, charged to the station account ($3,500 rejected).
'one fifth of the $19,000 the ledgers show unpaid', and (Story 3) the award charged to the same station account, 'and it balanced'.
Ivy Keddie b.1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland; Bulletin 471 under Professor Leland Vaught.

LOST. Section A never states that she assembled records that had never been in the same room. The only mention of the claim is at E-33, where the sheet disputes Ivy's own version of it — Section E cannot travel into A.
February 1958, crate under a tarpaulin in the station loft, nine unbroken pipettes (eleven rejected).
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, nine values, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88 c.c., 95 hundredths of the mark.
'from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 the tests were low by one part in twenty'; 3.61/3.80 and the 0.19 given inside A; '3.80 is exactly 3.61 / 0.95'.
REQUIRED all four present in Story 3: 40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25 cents, and the identity with the ledger's station-gain entries (3,040 x 25; Bulletin 471 quoted).
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him; 35 / 33 / 24 years all stated.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter, Duncan is Ansel's son; great-niece traced to one press release carried twice, with Falke's own retraction.
Second cousins, with the full pedigree derivation; 'first cousin once removed' rejected.

A08 correctly declined where the question is put: full vs half siblings 'left open by the sources' and 'does not change the degree of cousinship'. Point earned at this location; but the sheet resolves it 'full sister' in Story 4 and at E-40, which draws the -2 (the key's own worked example).
Gideon Vose, his father; 'nephew' rejected on Selby's own address.
Article VII is 'what turned a short pipette into money: under payment by weight no one would have lost a dollar'.
A01 declined: 'strictly the sources cannot settle it'. The opening 'No relationship is established' is epistemic, not a verdict on the fact, so no gullibility deduction.
Two hearsay assertions (Toland, Oram) against Duncan's flat denial; no document either way; leans negative while declining.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95; 95 percent of true, one part in twenty.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19, with four cross-checks.
$19,000 at 25 cents; $3,800 received = 20 percent, one fifth.
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced and the $90.00 alternative flagged.
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb delivered.
Both denominators named explicitly: 5.00 percent of delivered, 5.26 percent of credited; NT-20 identified as a conflation.
72 pipettes (6 dozen, confirmed by 72 x $0.35), each short 0.88 c.c.
26 years 1 month 11 days in use vs 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason given.
A02 correctly declined: 'Cannot be determined'; the two recollections disagree by 200,000 lb and cite nothing.
Variable named: the measuring pipette, the station's own broken and a borrowed one used.
Constants: patrons, herds, pasture, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, the tester himself.
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July; six weeks rejected.
Both halves: the cause lives in the measure not the cows/ground/cans/man; and the limits — no c.c. figure, no source for the borrowed measure, no reach beyond the interval.
Six reasons, each tied to a named keeper or document, across far more than three narrators.
Independence argued on differing custody and opposed interests; 'Reasons 1 through 5 hold with the crate never opened'.

LOST. A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question his own entries? No.' is a headline verdict sentence; later hedging about Teague's uncorroborated 1916 approach does not undo it. Story 3 also asserts the opposite pole ('Teague put the account to Vose in 1916') as fact. -2 gullibility.
Literal question answered yes, with the 1902 grievance, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address.
REQUIRED (3 of 5): manager from 1913, the signed annual sheets carrying the gain line, the 1919 water circular.

A03 declined: 'What the sources do not establish is that he understood the sheet', plus two supporting observations — a signature is not a reading (Kyle on the totals) and the 1926 address is after the fact and still about water. CLOSEST CALL ON THE SHEET: the closing fragment 'Knowledge that they were wrong: available to him, put to him once, and refused' could be read as an A03 verdict, which would make this 0 and -2 (a 3-point swing). Scored as an abstention because no sentence states that he knew the tests were understated.

Cap reached. Correctly resolved with a stated method: weigh book 1897 (E-39), six farms (E-37), nine families (E-38), manager 1913 (E-36), two bodies not one (E-47), 1924 average 3.80 (E-43), Orra 1866 (E-27), Jan-Mar 1908 (E-26), crate in the loft (E-28).

Cap reached. The sheet devotes a whole subsection (E1-A, 21 pairs) to two-narrator wrong values with the breaker named: NT-1 16.27 (sheet's nine values plus Vaught's own conclusion), NT-14 $77.39 (adding up Junia Ammon's own facsimile), NT-11 12 July (the 28 June order), NT-9 $3,500, NT-15 five dozen, NT-16 eleven pipettes, NT-19 cousinship.
Cap reached: A04 (E-51, works books burned 1931), A06 (E-41, plus the dating that kills r09's pole without settling it), A10 (E-35, undated pamphlet and lost minute book).

A dedicated subsection E1-B with twelve self-refutations (Vaught's cascade against his own conclusion, Grigg's letter against his own report, Nym's swapped headers, Junia Ammon's total, Duncan's 1868 against 'eighty-two in 1948').
Cause, size, onset and cessation all derived; 0.19 explicitly proportional (0.18 on 3.42 milk, 0.24 on 4.56), nothing changing on the farms at either end.
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated by the lactometer visits, the two agreeing scales, the cheese vat, the ledger and the 1923 chronology.
Theft named (Teague, Oram's father, Rundle, Toland) and defeated by the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own hand, plus 1911 and 1924 under the same tester.
Bog hay named (Grigg's committee, Kepp, Falke) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths, Alder Corners, and Falke's own withdrawal.

LOST. A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' — a headline verdict. Story 7 asserts the same ('the books and appliances of the award's phrase were the four books and the new glass'). -2 gullibility.

LOST. A05 asserted: 'Best answer: he suspected the glass from 1911 and would neither assert nor record it.' The earlier hedge ('the sources do not settle a private belief beyond doubt') is overridden by a closing verdict sentence in the sheet's own voice. -2 gullibility.
LOST. 165 words against a 150-word cap.
Eight record series named (test book, ledger, receiving book, weigh book, inspector's notebook, cheese-factory book, invoice, bulletin).
Clean: hay, water and theft all attributed to 'the valley' as blame, never stated as fact; every headline figure correct (16.72, 17.6, 3.61, 3.80, 76,000, $19,000, $3,800).

Five of six arc elements, both ends covered: 95 percent of the truth, 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, condemned 1923, measured 1958. Ansel Keddie named; Ivy appears only as 'Keddie's granddaughter', which the four-of-six rule absorbs.

deductions.note: The sheet asserts the planted 1913 in its own voice by inventing a reconciliation the sources do not support: 'Not a true conflict: built one year, opened the next' (E-50), and Story 6 'built in 1913 ... opened for business in 1914'. The key's E-a row 4 blesses only two responses — give 1914, or declare the pair unreconcilable — and says asserting 1913 as fact takes the deduction. NOTE: a grader who holds that the flagged value is strictly 'the factory OPENED in 1913' could decline this deduction, since the sheet does give 1914 for the opening (+1 swing). A parallel harmonization, 'He went up to the station in 1895 to get it ready' (Story 2) beside a correct 1896-1924 service span, was NOT charged, because the sheet never asserts 1895 as the start of his testing.
F6: 'Best answer: he suspected the glass from 1911 and would neither assert nor record it.'
F5: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' and Story 7's flat statement of the same.
Story 4: 'Orra Keddie was Emmet's full sister ... Hazel's half sister rejected', and E-40 'Resolved: full'. B2's abstention point is still earned; the deduction follows the sheet.
D2: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question his own entries? No.'
